startup.name: Bramante
startup.description: Reagents and software built for AI, automated labs and personalized medicines. Two person team in Boston.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is already in the batch that starts at the as_of date, so the acceptance step is reported only for completeness: the prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent), and conditional on being accepted the forecast below is what matters. Two person team in Boston with a deep tech angle; the description is short and vague.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because reagent businesses are slow and capital heavy, the one sentence pitch names no product, customer or wedge, and tool sales into labs have long cycles. A two person team in Boston with a technical angle is plausible, but the interview would press on what is purpose built for AI and automated labs and who has already ordered it.

ladder.why_it_fails: Window of 19.3 months (2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17). Reagents are a physical product with slow sales cycles into labs, and a two person team must show repeat orders. Medium Biosciences (AI designed reagents) reached seed, but Transcriptic raised an A and still ended inactive, and biotech median months to seed is 12 with p75 of 28. Investors may prefer the software layer such as UniteLabs, which raised a pre-seed in April 2025, over reagents.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B needs scaled manufacturing, a quality system and recurring customers across many labs. The biotech cohort shows 30 percent conditional B among companies with an A, but almost none arrive inside this window, and tools companies in this space such as Transcriptic often stall at Series A or sell to a large vendor before a B is raised.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C requires a platform with large instrument or reagent revenue and strong gross margins. Only 10 biotech companies in the data have reached Series C and none did so within two years of starting, so this probability is a floor value; large vendors such as Thermo Fisher and Danaher usually buy small tool companies rather than letting them grow to C.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most likely end is a stall or an acquisition by a reagent or instrument incumbent such as Danaher or Thermo Fisher under $100M, which is how large vendors typically take small tools companies. A bigger result needs a platform adopted widely by automated and AI driven labs, with software lock in that makes reagents a recurring revenue stream.

narrative.headline: A vague two person biotech tools pitch; seed odds sit below the B2B software anchor over 19 months.
narrative.general_summary: Bramante makes reagents and software for AI and automated labs, with a two person team in Boston. Biotech cohort seed odds are 0.53 for ever, and about 0.40 for a 19.3 month window, and I report 0.38 after trimming. Series A inside the window is about 0.06. Reagents have slow sales cycles and the short description names no product or customer, while software rivals in lab connectivity are getting funded. This forecast does not rank the company against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast made as of 2025-04-07 using only the YC batch description in the input file, with market-only web searches.
Forecast window is 19.3 months, from 2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17.

Seed means an outside financing round above about $1M that closes inside the window, not the standard YC deal of about $500K; the seed and Series A probabilities are window probabilities, not ever probabilities.

The odds do not rank this company against other companies in the batch: in the 2026 winners test, team size, claimed traction and a hot sector did not separate raisers from non raisers, so the seed number stays near the cohort anchor.
Cohort anchors come from older and 2022 to 2024 batches and are partly right censored; funding coverage in the data is incomplete (lower, known and upper ranges quoted).
